title: Repo market networks: dynamics under financial stress
summary: This ECB Working Paper analyzes the resilience of the euro-denominated repo market using transaction-level data and network analysis from 2021 to mid-February 2025. The research finds that the euro repo market exhibits a core-periphery structure, with connectivity intensifying during stress periods. Counter to expectations, financial stress is associated with lower repo spreads at the market level, indicating the market functions as a shock absorber rather than amplifying stress.
key_points: The euro repo market displays a core-periphery structure, with a small core of highly active institutions conducting most trading and a larger group of less active participants
Network connectivity between institutions, especially bank-to-bank trading, has increased over time, including during stress periods
Trading volumes and repo spreads remain broadly stable at the sectoral level under financial stress
At the market level, financial stress is associated with lower repo spreads, consistent with the market functioning as a shock absorber
The repo market accounts for 56% of daily transactions and 30% of outstanding amounts in the euro money market
The secured repo segment has doubled in daily turnover over the last decade, while the unsecured interbank segment has contracted to one-tenth of its former size
Financial stress is measured using the Composite Indicator of Systemic Stress (CISS)
why_it_matters: Understanding how repo market networks function during stress is critical for financial stability oversight. The finding that the euro repo market acts as a shock absorber—reducing spreads under stress—suggests the market has structural resilience, but policymakers must still monitor the core-periphery dynamics where concentrated activity in a few institutions could create vulnerabilities. The growing role of NBFIs in these markets adds systemic importance to these findings.
market_structure_context: The paper directly addresses market structure through network analysis of repo market counterparties. Key structural findings: (1) core-periphery architecture where connectivity intensifies during stress; (2) secured segment dominance (56% of daily transactions) has grown at the expense of unsecured interbank markets; (3) bank-to-bank connections have strengthened over time; (4) the market exhibits pricing resilience under stress with spreads compressing. Data from Securities Financing Transactions Data Store (SFTDS) covers 2021 through mid-February 2025.
